in_text_mentions: The site of onset of symptoms is usually the abdomen, often within striae distensae and with an intensely pruritic urticarial rash with erythematous, edematous papules, and plaques (Figure 3). Sparing of the umbilical region is a characteristic finding. The disease spreads to other body sites such as proximal thighs, buttocks, and the back. Rarely the eruption spreads ideally involving arms and legs [9]. The morphology changes while the disease advances, developing polymorphic features such as papulovesicles, erythema, and annular wheals.

plate_findings.evidence: perivascular interstitial lymphohistiocytic inflammation (in-text) / associated eosinophils and lymphocytes (caption)

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: H&E punch biopsy from polymorphic eruption of pregnancy case with bullae formation; caption attributes intraepidermal/subcorneal vesicle with eosinophils/lymphocytes and papillary dermal edema to panels A-C, in-text adds perivascular interstitial lymphohistiocytic inflammation supporting PUPPP histology. Bullous vesicle formation is unusual for PUPPP, hence atypical. B: x10 H&E clearly shows intraepidermal/subcorneal vesicle with eosinophils/lymphocytes and papillary dermal edema in PUPPP bullous case; in-text perivascular lymphohistiocytic inflammation supports vocabulary histology finding. Bullous presentation atypical. C: x20 H&E shows eosinophils/lymphocytes, papillary dermal edema and perivascular lymphohistiocytic inflammation in PUPPP bullous case; supports vocabulary histology finding. High-power detail of same atypical vesicular/bullous PUPPP biopsy.

plate_findings.evidence: Scattered erythematous urticoid papules coalescing into 2-3 cm plaques on an erythematous base on the abdomen and bilateral upper thighs (a)
Scattered erythematous urticoid papules coalescing into 2-3 cm plaques on an erythematous base on the abdomen and bilateral upper thighs (a)

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Panel A shows pregnant abdomen and thighs with erythematous papules coalescing into plaques, matching captioned PUPPP/polymorphic eruption of pregnancy in disease-focused article. B: Panel B shows lateral trunk with scattered erythematous urticoid papules coalescing into plaques, panel-specific caption attribution to polymorphic eruption of pregnancy. C: Panel C shows upper arm with erythematous papules/plaques, panel-specific caption attribution to polymorphic eruption of pregnancy. D: Panel D shows bilateral legs with papules/plaques, panel-specific caption attribution to polymorphic eruption of pregnancy with spread to lower extremities.

Given the morphology of pruritic urticoid papules with onset shortly before delivery and worsening thereafter, a diagnosis of PEP was made.
